notable_absence.finding: Across all ~40 documented Public API operations, exactly ONE declares an RBAC-role requirement at all: the deprecated, explicitly 'non-functional' CouchDB-compatibility stub POST /{db}/_ensure_full_commit, which states 'Required Sync Gateway RBAC roles: Sync Gateway Application / Sync Gateway Application Read Only' (verbatim) - roles belonging to the sgw:rbac-user identity system round 27 found governs only the Admin/Metrics API and is explicitly disjoint from the Public API's sgw:user. This single mention, on an endpoint the page itself calls non-functional and deprecated since CouchDB 3.0, corroborates round 27's split (the Public API otherwise never mentions RBAC roles at all) while looking like a documentation-generation artifact - likely schema metadata copied from an Admin API operation definition - rather than a real behavioural requirement. Separately, the 'Unsupported' tag groups two unrelated kinds of non-production surface under one label with no distinguishing structure: CouchDB-style design-document/view endpoints (retained for legacy compatibility, Admin-API-restricted) and a full OpenID Connect mock-provider/login/token flow that exists purely for Sync Gateway's own test suite (gated behind the unsupported oidc_test_provider flag) - a production API reference documenting seven endpoints whose sole purpose is simulating an external identity provider for tests.

cross_component_finding: sgw:all-channels-property's own registry description states it is 'Exposed as a first-class, queryable Admin-REST-API surface specifically because this union cannot be read off any single stored field' - but this page shows the identical computed structure (userCtx.channels, the same {"!": 1, "channelA": 2} per-channel sequence-number shape) returned by the Public API's Session resource (GET/POST /{db}/_session) as well, to the authenticated user themselves rather than an admin caller. The same computed effective-channel-set data is therefore exposed on two structurally different surfaces for two different audiences (admin introspection vs. a user checking their own access) - an alsoExposedAs pair, matching the pattern the registry already uses for the query system-keyspace/REST-admin surfaces. Also: the Replication tag is described as 'Create and manage inter-Sync Gateway replications', but its single documented endpoint (GET /{db}/_blipsync) explicitly serves BOTH Couchbase Lite (client=cbl2) and Sync-Gateway-to-Sync-Gateway (client=sgr2) traffic - the tag's own description undersells what the endpoint actually does, and the REST changes-feed (poll/longpoll/continuous/websocket, reused as sgw:changes-feed) is a wholly separate mechanism from this BLIP/websocket replication protocol, despite both moving 'changes' between peers.
cross_product_finding: The dual revision-identifier scheme is visible end-to-end at the Public REST API surface, not just internally: every document read/write/changes-feed/attachment endpoint accepts or returns both the Revision Tree ID (_rev, promoted as sgw:revision-tree) and the Current Version ID (_cv, promoted as sgw:version-vector) as alternative, explicitly-ordered optimistic-concurrency-control sources ('Precedence when multiple are present: rev query parameter, then If-Match header, then body _cv, then body _rev'). This confirms sgw:version-vector's registry note that it reuses Couchbase Server XDCR's Hybrid Logical Vector implementation is not merely an internal storage detail - the CV identifier format is a first-class, externally addressable value Couchbase Lite and ISGR clients read and supply through this API, giving Sync Gateway's document-versioning surface the same vocabulary Couchbase Server's own Cross Cluster Versioning (XDCR) exposes.
